sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Simulator 12.8A: W3C PROV-O Lineage Graph and Nilpotent Blast Radius Studio! Click on pipeline entities and activities to inspect provenance relationships, and compute matrix powers to trace the exact downstream blast radius.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Look at the adjacency matrix heatmap! As we raise matrix A to higher powers, the non-zero entries reveal every multi-hop path. By power 4, the matrix is completely zero, proving our DAG is strictly acyclic!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 12.8.1: Nilpotent Adjacency Matrix and Blast Radius Derivation. Given a five-vertex DAG with edges from v1 to v2, v2 to v3, and v3 to v4, evaluate the reachability matrix R and determine the downstream blast radius if raw web logs v1 is corrupted.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: Dr. Nova, if v1 connects to v2, v2 to v3, and v3 to v4, how many matrix powers do we need to calculate before the nilpotency condition collapses the series to zero?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding! The path depth is 3, so A to the fourth power equals zero. The reachability row for v1 shows non-zero paths to v2, v3, and v4, while v5 remains completely unpoisoned!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. In a 4-hop chain, A to the 4th is zero. The reachability matrix R equals I plus A plus A squared plus A cubed. The downstream reach of v1 contains v2, v3, and v4.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Welcome to Simulator 12.8B: Column-Level Semiring and Feature Poisoning Studio! Toggle individual source records to inspect the How-provenance polynomial, and trigger emergency quarantines to isolate affected production models.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Notice how the provenance polynomial cleanly separates alternative derivation paths! When record y1 is purged under GDPR, the output feature still survives through token z1!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 12.8.2: Semiring How-Provenance Polynomial Derivation. For an inner join of tables R and S unioned with table T, derive the provenance polynomial for id 10, and determine if the record survives when y1 is deleted under GDPR.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: In relational algebra, joins multiply provenance tokens while unions add them. If y1 is zeroed out, does the whole polynomial collapse or does z1 preserve the tuple?

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Spot-on! The polynomial is x1 times y1 plus x2 times y1 plus z1. Setting y1 to zero eliminates the join terms, but z1 preserves the record!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. By Green's semiring algebra, the inner join multiplies tuples yielding (x1 + x2) times y1, while UNION ALL adds z1. When y1 equals 0, z1 remains non-zero.

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Active Checkpoint 12.8.3: Column-Level Lineage versus Table-Level Blast Radius. Compare the Poisoning Impact Ratio when isolating corruption to a single column versus discarding the entire containing table.

sentences.speaker: Kaito
sentences.text: If only user age is corrupted in a 20-column feature table, table-level lineage would discard all 8 downstream models, whereas column-level lineage only affects the one model using age!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Outstanding! Column-level AST lineage slashes the Poisoning Impact Ratio from 100 percent down to 12.5 percent, preventing unnecessary downtime for unaffected models!

sentences.speaker: Dr. Nova
sentences.text: Incorrect. Coarse table-level lineage forces a complete rollback of all 8 models (PIR = 1.0). Column-level AST lineage isolates the blast radius to only the 1 model consuming user age (PIR = 0.125).
